headlines.title: ASML Soars 10% in a Week as Chip Stocks Bounce and Musk’s Terafab Eyes a Million Wafers
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysASML stock is up 10% in the past week as chip stocks rebounded and Musk’s Terafab reportedly set a target of 1 million wafers a month. Applied Materials and TSMC gained even more, so most of ASML’s jump came with the group.

headlines.title: Big Tech Will Spend “Well Over $1 Trillion” in 2027, Says Applied Materials CFO
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysApplied Materials CFO Brice Hill expects cloud capex to rise more than 50% in 2027 to well over $1 trillion. Customers want more tools than Applied can ship.

headlines.title: Applied Materials (AMAT) Stock Slips After Record Q4 Earnings Results
headlines.summary: Applied Materials just reported record Q4 2026 numbers, yet the stock slipped 2.8% to US$370.25 by Friday’s close. That reflects investor emotion running ahead of the spreadsheet. Revenue for the quarter was US$10.4b, with basic EPS at US$3.43, capping a fiscal year that management described as record on both sales and earnings. Investors came into this report after a choppy stretch, with the share price down over 17% in the past month and almost 27% over three months.

headlines.title: Applied Materials earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Applied Materials (AMAT) reported fiscal Q4 2026 on Nov 12, 2026 and beat on every headline line. The stock still fell. It trades at $367.76 (-3.46%) as of Nov 13, 2:53 PM EST, after the after-hours pop faded. The shares are down 20.8% over one month and 31.2% over three months. They sit far below the 52-week high of $739.67 and remain +64.7% over one year.

description: Applied Materials, Inc. provides materials engineering solutions, equipment, services, and software to the semiconductor and related industries in the United States, China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through Semiconductor Systems and Applied Global Services (AGS) segments. The Semiconductor Systems segment includes semiconductor capital equipment to enable materials engineering steps, including etch, rapid thermal processing, deposition, chemical mechanical planarization, metrology and inspection, wafer packaging, and ion implantation. The AGS segment offers integrated solutions to optimize equipment and fab performance and productivity comprising spares, upgrades, services, and 200 millimeter and other equipment and factory automation software for semiconductor and other products. It serves manufacturers of semiconductor wafers and chips, and other electronic devices. Applied Materials, Inc. was incorporated in 1967 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
